name: basic
why: The CSV path builds a Route with NO name and NO elevation, and does NOT call AdjustStartAndEnd (ridewithgps.py:235-238) -- materially different output from the JSON path for the same route.

script.body:
Type,Notes,Distance,Elevation,Description
Start,Start of route,0.0,0,
Right,Turn right on A,1.0,10,
Left,Turn left on B,2.0,20,note here

name: header_pruned
why: rows[1:] drops the first row unconditionally (ridewithgps.py:229), so a headerless CSV silently loses its first cue.

script.body:
Start,Start of route,0.0,0,
Right,Turn right on A,1.0,10,

name: embedded_newline_in_quoted_field
why: The body is split on '\n' BEFORE csv.DictReader sees it (ridewithgps.py:226). DictReader still reassembles the quoted field by pulling the next list item, so the row is NOT torn apart -- but the newline inside the field is silently swallowed, and 'Turn right,\nthen immediately left' arrives as 'Turn right,then immediately left' with no separator.

script.body:
Type,Notes,Distance,Elevation,Description
Right,"Turn right,
then immediately left",1.0,10,

name: trailing_blank_line
why: A trailing newline produces an empty final row.

name: not_modified_304
why: Same conditional-GET contract as the JSON path.

name: html_instead_of_csv
why: What the live endpoint returns TODAY: ridewithgps.com/routes/<id>.csv serves an HTML page, with or without api_key, so this function is dead against the real service. It does fail rather than producing garbage -- but with a bare TypeError from float(None), not a RideWithGpsError, so the web layer reports it as the generic 0xFA 'Error querying RideWithGPS' page.
